newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas mostly up late on technicals, cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas mostly up late on technicals, cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures mostly moved higher late Friday in moderate trade, still helped by a steady-to-firmer weekend cash market and some follow-through technical buying, industry sources said.
At 1430 EDT, May climbed 1.7 cents to $2.26 per million British thermal units, while June was 2.4 cents higher at $2.285. Most other months were steady to up 2.5 cents.

"Technically, all the moving averages point up and we've been piling on open interest. And in the cash, I think most people played May the way they played April - short," said one Houston trader, noting record Hub open interest Thursday.
Traders said recent declines in the year-on-year storage surplus coupled with improved technicals helped drive cash and futures up sharply this week.
But some said the top may be near, noting the market was overbought and due for a pullback after a nine percent rally in four days.
Chart traders pegged next resistance in June at $2.33 and then at the $2.385 contract high. Support was seen at $2.17, then at $2.05 and along the up trendline at $2.01.

In the cash, Gulf Coast weekend prices were steady to up slightly Friday in the $2.15-20 range. Midcon pipes were off a couple of cents to about $2. New York city gate gas was talked on either side of $2.45, flat from Thursday's levels.

Cooler weekend temperatures are forecast for most of the U.S. before returning to seasonal levels early next week in the central U.S. Warmer-than-normal weather was expected to continue in most of the Southwest and hit Texas next week.
NYMEX said 25,980 contracts traded at 1400 EDT.
On the KCBT, June firmed two cents to $2.10, while deferreds were steady to three cents higher. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.3 cent to 16.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
